data.why: The app bundles asterank_exo.csv as its own fallback dataset and loads it automatically when the (unreachable) Asterank API fails; there is no upload interface, so nothing needs to be copied or synthesized.

goals: Identify which Kepler planets fall into the 'promising' habitability status based on temperature and gravity
Examine how planet equilibrium temperature relates to orbital distance, grouped by host star size
Map candidate planets by celestial position (RA/Dec) to see sky distribution of habitability classes
Compare each planet's relative orbital distance (A/RSTAR) against Earth's reference ratio of 1.0
Explore which stellar mass/temperature regimes are associated with potentially habitable planets

review.summary: The tree matches the README's purpose and the code. It covers loading, filtering, all four charts and the table at a sensible depth, and 7 of the 9 screens I opened fully support their nodes. It needs small fixes before filing: re-cite the PNG-export evidence, explain the hidden habitability thresholds and the inconsistent colours in the Relative Distance chart, and correct one incomplete action label.
